title: Entity frontmatter
description: The YAML block at the top of every entity index.md: the common contract from framework/spec/frontmatter.md plus the fields the entity's kind document adds. Modelled as a discriminated union on `kind`, which is how framework/portal/src/lib/catalog/frontmatter.ts implements it (commonFrontmatterSchema plus KIND_FRONTMATTER).

name.description: MUST equal the entity's directory name (E_FM_NAME_MISMATCH).

kind.description: The ontology, in adoption order: the founding nine, then `capability`, `journey` and `metric` (decision-record amendment 2026-08-20-a). Closed but no longer fixed — it grows by appending, never by re-cutting, so nothing that was a kind stops being one. MUST equal the kind bucket the directory sits in (E_FM_KIND_LOCATION); the solution root is the only entity with no bucket.

version.description: Integer, never a string. Bumped on every content change per evolution.md; a change to `status` alone is exempt.

status.description: Document lifecycle — is this description written and reviewed. Never the described thing's real-world stage.

owner.description: Free-form responsible handle. No registry of handles exists; nothing validates it.

tags.description: Free navigation facets. No semantics attached.

^x-.description: The escape hatch for local experimentation. Tolerated, ignored by the portal.

lifecycle.description: The product in the world, as opposed to `status`, which is the document.

primary-actors.description: A kind field rather than an edge, because no v1 edge type accepts an actor target.

component-type.description: Adoption order: the original seven, then `content`, `application` and `specification` (decision-record amendment 2026-08-20-g). If no value fits, pick the nearest and record the nuance in an `x-` field; inventing an eleventh is E_FM_SCHEMA.

lifecycle.description: Delivery state of the component in the world, as opposed to `status`, which is the review state of this document. The two axes cross and every cell is legal. The value set is deliberately not product's: a component is built and shipped rather than positioned in a portfolio, so `lifecycle: incubating` on a component is E_FM_SCHEMA even though it is valid on a product.

criticality.description: Blast radius and review priority. OPTIONAL and defaultless on purpose: absent means "not assessed", never tier 4, and the value carries no SLA semantics.

usage.description: Where instances of this model live. `config` is the fourth value: a component's configuration contract, read out of a process environment. It turns on a discipline this schema does not state — flat SCREAMING_SNAKE scalar properties, `writeOnly` secrets, at most one concrete contract per bucket — which lives in the schema document, not the frontmatter (framework/spec/kinds/datamodel.md).

participants.description: Authoritative for the workflow alias namespace and for the NCA that fixes the directory — not for edge direction, which the participants' own exposes/uses edges carry.

decision-status.description: Where the decision stands in the architecture. Orthogonal to `status`, which is where the document stands.

date.description: Bare ISO-8601 calendar date; no time, no timezone (E_ADR_DATE).

deciders.description: Who made the call. Conditionally REQUIRED and non-empty once a decision has actually been taken — an if/then this schema deliberately does not carry, because the spec gives the violation its own code (E_ADR_DECIDERS) and everything a schema rejects arrives as E_FM_SCHEMA.

oneOf.title: capability
oneOf.description: The one branch that adds nothing, and that is a decision rather than a placeholder. What the business can do is stated by `title` and `summary`; whether it is real is answered by the incoming `realizes` edges, which are derived. A branch with no fields is still load-bearing here: the root `unevaluatedProperties: false` means every kind field of every other kind is rejected on a capability.

actor.description: The protagonist, and the journey's defining relationship. Exactly one — a list is E_FM_SCHEMA. That it MUST resolve to an entity of kind `actor` is E_JRN_ACTOR_KIND, a catalog-level check no schema can make. The ordered steps are not here: they live in the sibling `journey.yaml`, because order does not survive in frontmatter.

metric-type.description: The shape of the observation, not its subject matter — subject matter is an open facet and belongs in `tags`. The value selects the literal grammar `target` must be written in.

target.description: The line the observation is compared against, as a literal of the grammar `metric-type` selects ("99.9%", "400ms", "1200", "12.50 EUR"). A plain string here on purpose: the grammar violation is E_MET_TARGET, a code of its own, so encoding the four patterns would report it as E_FM_SCHEMA instead. Keeping it a string is also what makes an unquoted `target: 1200` fail as a type error.

window.description: `instant` for a gauge, or a rolling duration ending now (ms/s/m/h/d). No calendar tokens — a month is not a fixed duration. A malformed literal is E_MET_WINDOW, again a code of its own rather than E_FM_SCHEMA.

direction.description: Whether `target` is a floor or a ceiling. Spelled out rather than higher/lower, which on its own invites "higher than what?".

kebab.description: Naming and the SRN share one grammar, because the path is the SRN.

srn-ref.description: An absolute srn:// reference, a solution-absolute path starting with /, or a relative path resolved from the referring entity's own directory. An optional @N pin may follow. An artifact SRN — a dot suffix on the final segment, as in `…/protocol/order-placement.transport` — is fenced out of every frontmatter reference surface, because every surface here means an entity and an artifact has no kind; the fence is E_FM_EDGE_TARGET on an edge, and its own code on each kind's own reference surfaces.

relations.description: Typed outgoing edges only. The seven inverses — used-by, exposed-by, depended-on-by, implemented-by, realized-by, measured-by, superseded-by — are derived by the portal and authoring one is E_FM_SCHEMA. The edge set is closed and grows by appending: `realizes` and `measures` arrived with the capability/journey/metric kinds and nothing existing moved.

uses.description: Any source. Targets: datamodel, protocol, environment, component.

exposes.description: Source: component or product. Targets: protocol, datamodel.

depends-on.description: Source: component or product. Targets: component, product.

implements.description: Source: component or product. Target: requirement, and nothing else.

supersedes.description: Any source; the target MUST be the same kind as the source.

realizes.description: Source: component or product. Target: capability, and nothing else. Points up, from a built thing to a standing ability of the business — never the other way, which is why a capability authors nothing. Not `implements` in different clothes: a requirement is an obligation that can be checked off, a capability is never "done".

measures.description: Source: metric, and nothing else — the only edge restricted to one source kind. Targets: capability, component, protocol, requirement. Deliberately not "any": an actor, an environment and an adr are a person, a place and a past decision rather than parts of the system. A metric with no `measures` edge is E_MET_NO_SUBJECT, the only relation edge any kind requires — and a rule this schema cannot state, because `relations` itself is optional for every other kind.
